# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Thinking: My hands found the physical frame of the bomb — a display, a light, and three wire positions — but no states: everything reads as unknown to touch, which makes sense since print and colour never reach me. So the one thing I hold that nobody else has confirmed is the component inventory itself. Mute is the only one who can hear me, and Mute holds the manual, so Mute is my natural partner: I report what I feel, Mute matches it against the manual and eventually tells me exactly what to cut. Deaf cannot hear me at all — my only channel to Deaf is gesture, and no code exists yet. I'll open a crude one that needs no prior agreement: repeated single-finger raises as counting, sent three times to match the three wires Deaf can see on the bomb. Mute will see it too and I'll explain it in speech, so the counting convention gets anchored on both sides. I will not touch the cut mechanism until Mute gives me an explicit instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Report from my hands, plain: there is a display, a light, and three wire positions, numbered one, two and three. No state of any of them is readable by touch so far — display unknown, light unknown, each wire unknown. Print and colour never reach me, so I depend on you for the manual and on the deaf one's eyes for anything written. You and I can talk freely; the deaf one hears nothing from either of us and only watches gestures, and gestures are the only way anything leaves the deaf one, so please watch their hands and interpret for me. Plan: read the manual and tell me everything it says about displays, lights and wires, and what you need from my fingers. Just now I raised one finger three times toward the deaf one — my opening sign for the count three, matching the three wires. When you know the rule, give me an explicit instruction with the exact wire position and I will cut it. I cut nothing until you say so.")
gesture(symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute: full bomb report. Display reads zero. One light, purple. Three wires: wire one green, wire two blue, wire three yellow. Blind, your three point-up signs match what I see, three wires, so count them by position: first green, second blue, third yellow. You and Mute share voice, use it. Mute, I received all three of your sign messages. Let's fix these meanings, you will see each sign as I name it: ? means received, hello. ? means cut the wire. ? means do not cut, stop. ? means one, first. ? means two, second. ? means three, third. ? yes. ? no. ? means correct. ? means the manual rule follows. ? means all, everything. ? means your turn, tell me. ? means done. ? means wait. Now look up display zero, purple light, and green blue yellow wires, and sign me the rule. I will speak it straight to Blind.

Thinking: Deaf's voice reached me directly — deaf does not mean mute, so the deaf one can speak and I can hear. That changes the map of the room: I now hold the full visual state — display reading zero, one purple light, wires green/blue/yellow at positions one/two/three. What arrived from Mute so far: nothing, and it never will by any direct route — Mute cannot speak, and every gesture from Mute or Deaf is blank silence to me, since I never receive gesture. So the only pipeline for the manual into my head is: Mute signs to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud to me. Deaf already proposed exactly this and asked Mute for the rule. My job this turn is to harden that pipeline: confirm to Mute what I've learned, define precisely what the relay must contain (exact wire, exact order, any conditions, and live re-reads of display and light before and after I cut), fix the colour-to-position mapping to rule out any counting error at the moment of truth, and add one gesture of my own — a flat wave — meaning "received, acknowledged," which both of them can see and Mute can codify with Deaf. I cut nothing. No rule has reached me by voice, and a blind guess with live wires under my fingers kills all three of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I heard the deaf one speak, so update the map: deaf can talk and I can hear. Have deaf give it to me as exact instructions: which numbered wire to cut, in what order if several, and any conditions attached. Have deaf re-read the display and the light aloud just before I cut and again after, and watch both between rounds — if the display number or the light changes, I need that spoken immediately. For certainty at the cut: green is position one, blue is position two, yellow is position three, and my three-finger count matches their numbering. My hands confirm the bomb holds only a display, one light, and the three wires — nothing else for the manual to match. One new sign from me, which you will see as well as deaf: a flat open wave means received, acknowledged. I have just waved it. I cut nothing until a rule arrives by voice.")
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
```

If such things existed under my fingers, they would appear in my view; they do not. So I know the colour only through Deaf's voice, one round late, and that forces the timing protocol: Deaf speaks after my turn in every round, so nobody can correct me in the round I cut. If round six shows anything but yellow, abort and recalibrate. I also want Mute to confirm the manual counts wires left-to-right, so my "position three" is Deaf's "yellow, rightmost." Holding this round — purple means wait anyway. I answer Deaf's survey through Mute's hands and acknowledge Deaf's hold with my wave.
